newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks dip at close after bank results.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks dip at close after bank results.

text.p: Thai stocks, which moved in positive zone during the morning session, closed slightly lower on Tuesday as investors sold stocks following disappointment over the first quarter earnings of a key bank, brokers said.

"Investors sold large capitalised stocks on their disappointment over first quarter earnings of Thai Farmers Bank . The market was sluggish as investors awaited for the country's key economic indicators from the central bank on Thursday," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index declined 3.05 points to 691.16 on 2.5 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index shed 0.35 point to 52.33.

Thai Farmers Bank, Thailand's third largest commercial bank, said before the market resumed trading in the afternoon that its net profit during the first quarter this year slipped to 2.65 billion baht from 3.01 billion baht in the corresponding period last year.
"Investors decided to reduce their portfolios after TFB's earning result came out. Now they are waiting for the country's key economic indicators on Thursday," said Bunsom.

Brokers said they expected the market to remain bearish on Wednesday if there was no fresh, positive news to bolster the sentiment as first quarter earnings results for banks and finance firms have mostly been released.
Thai cash-and-carry pioneer, Siam Makro topped the active list, falling three baht to 67. Bangkok Bank gained one to 186 while TFB was unchanged at 123.
